newsitem.title: USA: Witness sees Conrail breach of duty in deal.
newsitem.headline: Witness sees Conrail breach of duty in deal.

text.p: Conrail Inc's board of directors breached their duty to the company's interest in their agreement to merge with CSX Corp, a witness told a U.S. District Court hearing on Monday
Norfolk Southern Corp is seeking to block a CSX tender offer for 19.9 percent of Conrail shares.

Furthermore, he said, Conrail agreed to a structure of the bid which will effectively enable CSX to gain control of Conrail once it has succeeded with the $110 per share tender offer, which expires Wednesday.
"The merger will be a 'fait accompli'," Coffee said, arguing that a 19.9 percent CSX stake will effectively stampede other investors into approving the rest of the deal.

However, some takeover stock specialists have said that unless CSX increases its offer, shareholders will defeat in a December meeting a waiver in Conrail's charter designed to allow the deal to proceed.

Attorneys for CSX and Conrail, in cross-examining Coffee, sought to show that Conrail did not act to manipulate the impending shareholder vote, and that takeover provisions in the merger agreement between CSX and Conrail have served to extract a higher price from CSX, as well as a higher rival bid from Norfolk Southern.

But Coffee countered by alluding to employment agreements for Conrail executives in the merger plan. He said that if Conrail had negotiated only in its shareholders interests rather than in the interests also of its management, "it might have been possible to get a considerably higher price."
Earlier in the hearing, U.S. District Judge Donald Van Artsdalen declined to rule on a motion by Conrail to dismiss NSC's complaint.

CSX has said it will pay $110 per share for 40 percent of Conrail, and exchange shares for the rest, in a bid worth an estimated $8.5 billion. The cash offer for 19.9 percent of Conrail shares, to expire Wednesday, is the first stem.
Coffee was the lead witness in the hearing, which is expected to last two days.

Coffee said the Conrail board improperly agreed to continue recommending a CSX offer to buy Conrail for 270 days regardless of other bids, and agreed not to amend its "poison pill" anti-takeover provisions for any offer other than CSX's.
